sentences.zh: 陳騫

translations.literal: Chen Qian
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qian

sentences.zh: 陳騫，臨淮東陽人也。

translations.literal: Chen Qian was a man of Dongyang in Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qian came from Dongyang in Linhuai commandery.

sentences.zh: 父矯，魏司徒。

translations.literal: His father was Chen Jiao, Minister of Education of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Chen Jiao, had served Wei as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 矯本廣陵劉氏，為外祖陳氏所養，因而改焉。

translations.literal: Jiao had originally belonged to the Liu clan of Guangling; he was adopted and brought up by his maternal grandfather's Chen family, and therefore changed his surname.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jiao was born into the Liu family of Guangling, his mother's Chen relatives raised him, and he took their surname.

sentences.zh: 騫沈厚有智謀。

translations.literal: Qian was steady, deep, and resourceful.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was reserved and thoughtful, with a gift for strategy.

sentences.zh: 初，矯為尚書令，侍中劉曄見幸于魏明帝，譖矯專權。

translations.literal: At first, when Jiao was Director of the Department of State Affairs, the Palace Attendant Liu Ye, who was favored by Emperor Ming of Wei, slandered Jiao for monopolizing power.
translations.idiomatic: While Jiao headed the Department of State Affairs, Palace Attendant Liu Ye enjoyed Emperor Ming of Wei's favor and accused Jiao of wielding unchecked authority.

sentences.zh: 矯憂懼，以問騫。

translations.literal: Jiao was anxious and afraid, and asked Qian about it.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Jiao sought Qian's advice.

sentences.zh: 騫曰：「主上明聖，大人大臣，今若不合意，不過不作公耳。

translations.literal: Qian said, 'The lord is enlightened and sage; the great man is a chief minister. If you now fail to please him, at worst you will not be made a duke.'
translations.idiomatic: Qian replied, 'The sovereign is wise, and you stand among the great ministers. Even if you fall from favor, the worst that happens is that you are not enfeoffed as a duke.'

sentences.zh: 」後帝意果釋，騫尚少，為夏侯玄所侮，意色自若，玄以此異之。

translations.literal: Later the emperor's resentment indeed eased. Qian was still young when Xiahou Xuan humiliated him; his expression remained calm, and Xuan therefore thought him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger soon passed. Qian was still a youth when Xiahou Xuan slighted him; he never lost his composure, and Xuan came to respect him for it.

sentences.zh: 起家尚書郎，遷中山、安平太守，並著稱績。

translations.literal: He began his career as a Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat and was promoted to Governor of Zhongshan and of Anping; in both commands he earned praise for his administration.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat to governor of Zhongshan and Anping, distinguishing himself in both posts.

sentences.zh: 徵為相國司馬、長史、禦吏中丞，遷尚書，封安國亭侯。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as Major to the Minister of State, Chief Clerk, and Palace Assistant Censor, then promoted to Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Marquis of the An'guo village.
translations.idiomatic: The court called him to be chief clerk and major under the minister of state and palace censor, then director of the Department of State Affairs, with a village marquisate at An'guo.

sentences.zh: 蜀賊寇隴右，以尚書持節行征蜀將軍，破賊而還。

translations.literal: When Shu forces raided Longyou, he bore the staff of authority as Director of the Department of State Affairs and acted as general for the campaign against Shu; he defeated the enemy and returned.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shu incursion into Longyou he led the expedition as acting general while holding his director's commission, routed the raiders, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 會諸葛誕之亂，復以尚書行安東將軍。

translations.literal: When Zhuge Dan rebelled, he was again, as Director of the Department of State Affairs, appointed acting General of the East.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhuge Dan's revolt he took the same minister's commission and served as acting General of the East.

sentences.zh: 壽春平，拜使持節、都督淮北諸軍事、安東將軍，進爵廣陵侯。

translations.literal: After Shouchun was pacified, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, area commander for all military affairs north of the Huai, and General of the East; his noble rank was advanced to Marquis of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouchun fell, he received the credentials of area commander north of the Huai and kept his eastern generalship, with his title raised to Marquis of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 轉都督豫州諸軍事、豫州刺史，持節、將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to area commander for all military affairs in Yuzhou and Governor of Yuzhou, retaining the staff of authority and his general's title.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on to command Yuzhou's armies and govern the province, still bearing the staff and his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 又轉都督江南諸軍事，徙都督荊州諸軍事、征南大將軍，封郯侯。

translations.literal: He was again made area commander south of the Yangzi, then transferred to area commander for Jingzhou and General Who Conquers the South, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: His command shifted to the southland, then to Jingzhou as General Who Conquers the South, with a marquisate at Tan.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，以佐命之勳，進車騎將軍，封高平郡公，遷侍中、大將軍，出為都督揚州諸軍事，餘如故，假黃鉞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, Qian was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry for his merit among the founding ministers, enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoping commandery, advanced to Palace Attendant and Grand General, and sent out as area commander for Yangzhou's armies, his other posts unchanged; he was also granted the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Yan founded the Jin, Qian's founding service earned him the chariots-and-cavalry command, the ducal fief of Gaoping, posts as palace attendant and grand general, command of Yangzhou, and the ceremonial axe that marked supreme delegated authority.

sentences.zh: 攻拔吳枳裏城，破塗中屯戍。

translations.literal: He stormed and took the Wu stronghold at Zhili and destroyed the garrison at Tuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Wu's Zhili fortress and dismantled the encampment at Tuzhong.

sentences.zh: 賜騫兄子惺爵關中侯。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed the noble rank of Marquis of Guanzhong on Qian's nephew Xing.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial grant raised Qian's nephew Xing to Marquis of Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，遷太尉，轉大司馬。

translations.literal: In the early Xianning era he was promoted to Grand Commandant, then to Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xianning reign he became Grand Commandant, then Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 騫因入朝，言於帝曰：「胡烈、牽弘皆勇而無謀，強于自用，非綏邊之材，將為國恥。

translations.literal: When Qian attended court he reported to the emperor: 'Hu Lie and Qian Hong are brave but lack strategy; they force their own way and are not fit to pacify the borders—they will disgrace the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: At audience Qian warned the throne that Hu Lie and Qian Hong were bold yet rash, unsuited to frontier settlement and apt to bring national shame.

sentences.zh: 願陛下詳之。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to weigh this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the sovereign to reconsider their appointments.

sentences.zh: 」時弘為揚州刺史，不承順騫命。

translations.literal: At the time Qian Hong was Governor of Yangzhou and refused to obey Qian's orders.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was then governor of Yangzhou and would not follow Qian's directives.

sentences.zh: 帝以為不協相構，於是征弘，既至，尋復以為涼州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor assumed the two men were feuding and slandering each other, so he summoned Hong; after Hong arrived he soon appointed him Governor of Liangzhou again.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler took their clash for mutual spite, recalled Hong, then almost immediately sent him west as governor of Liangzhou once more.

sentences.zh: 騫竊歎息，以為必敗。

translations.literal: Qian sighed to himself, convinced disaster would follow.
translations.idiomatic: Qian privately groaned, certain the policy would end badly.

sentences.zh: 二人後果失羌戎之和，皆被寇喪沒，征討連歲，僅而得定，帝乃悔之。

translations.literal: The two men afterward alienated the Qiang and Rong peoples; both died under barbarian attack, and campaigns dragged on for years before order was barely restored. The emperor then regretted his decision.
translations.idiomatic: Both later shattered tribal alliances, fell to raids, and cost years of campaigning before the frontier steadied—only then did the court regret ignoring Qian.

sentences.zh: 騫少有度量，含垢匿瑕，所在有績。

translations.literal: Qian had possessed forbearance since youth; he swallowed insults and overlooked faults, and wherever he served he left a record of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Qian bore slights lightly and governed effectively wherever he was posted.

sentences.zh: 與賈充、石苞、裴秀等俱為心膂，而騫智度過之，充等亦自以為不及也。

translations.literal: Together with Jia Chong, Shi Bao, Pei Xiu, and others he belonged to the emperor's inner circle, yet Qian's judgment surpassed theirs, and they conceded they could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: He stood with Jia Chong, Shi Bao, and Pei Xiu among the sovereign's closest advisers, but his political judgment exceeded theirs, as they themselves allowed.

sentences.zh: 累處方任，為士庶所懷。

translations.literal: Time and again he held regional authority, and both elites and commoners looked to him with trust.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated tours as a regional commander won him the confidence of scholar and commoner alike.

sentences.zh: 既位極人臣，年逾致仕，思欲退身。

translations.literal: Once he had climbed to a subject's highest rank and passed the age for retirement, he wished to step down.
translations.idiomatic: At the summit of a minister's career and past the usual age of retirement, he longed to withdraw.

sentences.zh: ，求入朝，因乞骸骨。

translations.literal: He asked leave to come to the capital and petitioned to retire on grounds of old age.
translations.idiomatic: He sought permission to return to Luoyang and yield his office, pleading age and infirmity.

sentences.zh: 賜袞冕之服，詔曰：「騫元勳舊德，統乂東夏，方弘遠績，以一吳會，而所苦未除，每表懇切，重勞以方事。

translations.literal: He was granted the highest ceremonial robe and cap, and an edict said: 'Qian, for his founding merit and long-tested virtue, has governed the eastern lands. We meant to rely on him for still greater deeds and to bring the Wu region to heel, yet the ailment that troubles him has not lifted, and every memorial is urgent and sincere, while we have again burdened him with frontier duties.
translations.idiomatic: The court invested him with ducal regalia and issued an edict praising his role in the east, explaining that though Wu remained unconquered and his illness lingered, his repeated pleas had forced military burdens upon him nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 今聽留京城，以前太尉府為大司馬府，增置祭酒二人，帳下司馬、官騎、大車、鼓吹皆如前，親兵百人，廚田十頃，廚園五十畝，廚士十人，器物經用皆留給焉。

translations.literal: Now we permit him to remain in the capital. The former Grand Commandant's compound shall serve as the Grand Marshal's mansion; add two libationers; adjutant majors, mounted escort, large wagons, and bands remain as before; assign a hundred household guards, ten qing of kitchen land, fifty mu of kitchen garden, ten kitchen servants, and leave all ordinary equipage in place.
translations.idiomatic: He was allowed to stay in Luoyang: his old grand commandant's offices became the grand marshal's residence, with added staff, guards, kitchen holdings, and household support left intact.

sentences.zh: 又給乘輿輦，出入殿中加鼓吹，如漢蕭何故事。

translations.literal: In addition he is granted use of an imperial palanquin and may enter and leave the palace with a military band, following the Han precedent for Xiao He.
translations.idiomatic: He could ride the imperial litter into the palace precincts with musicians, as Xiao He once had under the Han.

sentences.zh: 」騫累稱疾辭位，詔曰：「騫履德論道，朕所諮詢。

translations.literal: Qian repeatedly pleaded illness to resign from office, and an edict replied: 'Qian cultivates virtue and expounds the Way; he is one whom I consult.'
translations.idiomatic: When Qian again cited poor health, the throne insisted he remained indispensable for moral counsel and policy.

sentences.zh: 方賴謀猷，以弘庶績，宜時視事。

translations.literal: 'We depend on his counsel to enlarge the public good; he should return to his duties without delay.'
translations.idiomatic: The edict declared that the state still needed his plans and ordered him back to work.

sentences.zh: 可遣散騎常侍諭意。

translations.literal: 'Dispatch a Supernumerary Palace Attendant to convey our intent.'
translations.idiomatic: A supernumerary attendant would bear the emperor's wishes to him in person.

sentences.zh: 」騫輒歸第，詔又遣侍中敦諭還府。

translations.literal: Qian went straight home, and the court again sent a Palace Attendant to urge him sternly to return to headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Instead Qian retired to his house, prompting another round of messages from attendants pressing him to reopen his offices.

sentences.zh: 遂固請，許之，位同保傅，在三司之上，賜以几杖，不朝，安車駟馬，以高平公還第。

translations.literal: He pressed his request until it was granted. His rank equaled that of the elder tutors, standing above the Three Dukes; he received a seat and staff, was excused from court, given a comfortable carriage and four-horse team, and sent to his estate as Duke of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: At last his resignation stood: he was ranked above the three highest ministers like an imperial mentor, with chair, staff, freedom from court audience, a coach and four, and the title of Duke of Gaoping while living privately.

sentences.zh: 帝以其勳舊耆老，禮之甚重。

translations.literal: The emperor, honoring him as a founding elder, treated him with exceptional ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: As a dynastic founder now grown old, Qian received extraordinary deference from the throne.

sentences.zh: 又以騫有疾，聽乘輿上殿。

translations.literal: Because Qian was unwell, he was permitted to be carried in a litter into the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ill health won him the privilege of a litter right up to the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 騫素無謇諤之風，然與帝語傲；

translations.literal: Qian had never been outspoken, yet in speaking with the emperor he carried himself with pride;
translations.idiomatic: He was not known for blunt remonstrance, but he spoke to the sovereign with something like insolence,

sentences.zh: 及見皇太子加敬，時人以為諂。

translations.literal: when he met the crown prince he showed deference, and people of the day took it for flattery.
translations.idiomatic: yet before the heir apparent he became deferential, which contemporaries dismissed as sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 弟稚與其子輿忿爭，遂說騫子女穢行，騫表徙弟，以此獲譏於世。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhi quarreled with Zhi's son Yu, then spread scandal about the misconduct of Qian's children; Qian memorialized to have his brother banished, and the world ridiculed him for it.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother Zhi feuded with nephew Yu and aired lurid tales about Qian's sons and daughters, Qian used a memorial to exile Zhi—earning widespread scorn.

sentences.zh: 薨，年八十一，加以袞斂，贈太傅，諡曰武。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-one. He was buried in ducal vestments, posthumously honored as Grand Tutor, with the posthumous name Martial.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-one, laid out in princely robes, ennobled posthumously as Grand Tutor with the epithet "Martial."

sentences.zh: 及葬，帝于大司馬門臨喪，望柩流涕，禮依大司馬石苞故事。

translations.literal: At the burial the emperor came to the Grand Marshal Gate to mourn, gazed at the coffin and wept; the rites followed the precedent for Grand Marshal Shi Bao.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign mourned him at the Grand Marshal Gate, weeping over the bier as had been done for Grand Marshal Shi Bao.

sentences.zh: 子輿嗣爵。

translations.literal: His son Yu inherited the noble title.
translations.idiomatic: The marquisate passed to his son Yu.

translations.literal: The received text gives a lone equals sign between entries.
translations.idiomatic: The transmitted text preserves an equals sign used here as a sectional divider.

sentences.zh: 子輿

translations.literal: Yu
translations.idiomatic: Yu

sentences.zh: =輿字顯初，拜散騎侍郎、洛陽令，遷黃門侍郎，厲將校左軍、大司農、侍中。

translations.literal: Yu, courtesy name Xianchu, was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman of the Palace and Magistrate of Luoyang, promoted to Palace Attendant, and served successively as colonel of the left among the household guards, Minister of Agriculture, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu, style Xianchu, rose through supernumerary gentleman and Luoyang magistrate to palace attendant, then led the left colonel's corps, ran the Ministry of Agriculture, and returned to the palace corps.

sentences.zh: 坐與叔父不睦，出為河內太守。

translations.literal: Because he could not live peaceably with his uncle, he was sent out as Governor of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: A bitter break with his uncle cost him the capital and landed him in Henei as governor.

sentences.zh: 輿雖無檢正，而有力致。

translations.literal: Yu lacked strict rectitude, yet he possessed force and influence.
translations.idiomatic: He was no model of propriety, but he wielded real power.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，子植字弘先嗣，官至散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He died not long afterward; his son Zhi, courtesy name Hongxian, succeeded him and rose to Supernumerary Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after; his heir Zhi (Hongxian) reached the post of supernumerary attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，子粹嗣，永嘉中遇害，孝武帝以騫玄孫襲爵。

translations.literal: When Zhi died, his son Cui succeeded; in the Yongjia turmoil Cui was killed, and Emperor Xiaowu had Qian's great-grandson inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: The line ran Zhi to Cui until Yongjia partisans murdered Cui; Emperor Xiaowu then restored the title through a great-grandson of Qian.

sentences.zh: 卒，弟子浩之嗣。

translations.literal: When that heir died, his cousin Haozhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When this successor died, cousin Haozhi inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu accepted the Jin abdication, the marquisate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Song founder's usurpation ended the house's noble title.

sentences.zh: 裴秀

translations.literal: Pei Xiu
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiu

sentences.zh: 裴秀，字季彥，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Xiu, courtesy name Jiyan, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiu, style Jiyan, hailed from Wenxi county in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖茂，漢尚書令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mao had been Director of the Department of State Affairs under the Han.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mao once directed the Han Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 父潛，魏尚書令。

translations.literal: His father Qian had been Director of the Department of State Affairs under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian held the same office under Wei.

sentences.zh: 秀少好學，有風操，八歲能屬文。

translations.literal: Xiu loved learning from youth and cultivated integrity; at eight sui he could compose essays.
translations.idiomatic: He was bookish and principled even as a boy, composing polished prose at eight.

sentences.zh: 叔父徽有盛名，賓客甚眾。

translations.literal: His uncle Wei enjoyed great fame, and guests thronged his house.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle Wei attracted crowds of distinguished visitors.

sentences.zh: 秀年十餘歲，有詣徽者，出則過秀。

translations.literal: When Xiu was little more than ten, callers who visited Wei would stop to see Xiu on their way out.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was eleven, departing guests routinely paid their respects to young Xiu.

sentences.zh: 然秀母賤，嫡母宣氏不之禮，嘗使進饌於客，見者皆為之起。

translations.literal: Yet Xiu's mother was of low birth, and his father's principal wife, Lady Xuan, treated her coldly; she once sent her to serve food to guests, and everyone who saw it rose in respect.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiu's mother was a concubine of humble origin, Lady Xuan snubbed her and once made her wait on guests—yet visitors rose to honor the boy she bore.

sentences.zh: 秀母曰：「微賤如此，當應為小兒故也。

translations.literal: Xiu's mother said, 'To be humiliated so must be because of the little boy.'
translations.idiomatic: His mother murmured that such degradation came only from standing behind her gifted son.

sentences.zh: 」宣氏知之，後遂止。

translations.literal: When Lady Xuan understood, she ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lady Xuan grasped the point, the abuse stopped.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「後進領袖有裴秀。」

translations.literal: People of the time coined the saying, 'Among the rising generation the leader is Pei Xiu.'
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries summed it up: Pei Xiu led the younger set of talent.

sentences.zh: 渡遼將軍毌丘儉嘗薦秀于大將軍曹爽，曰：「生而岐嶷，長蹈自然，玄靜守真，性入道奧；

translations.literal: The General Who Crosses the Liao, Guanqiu Jian, once recommended Xiu to Grand General Cao Shuang: 'From birth he showed singular gifts; grown, he follows nature; still and pure, he holds fast to the true and his nature joins the depths of the Way.'
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian urged Cao Shuang to notice Xiu as a prodigy whose calm integrity plumbed the Dao itself.

sentences.zh: 博學強記，無文不該；

translations.literal: 'Broad in learning and strong of memory, there is no branch of letters he does not embrace.'
translations.idiomatic: The memorial praised his encyclopedic memory and mastery of every literary genre.

sentences.zh: 孝友著于鄉党，高聲聞於遠近。

translations.literal: 'Filial and fraternal at home, his lofty name carries far beyond his district.'
translations.idiomatic: It stressed his family virtue and reputation abroad.

sentences.zh: 誠宜弼佐謨明，助和鼎味，毗贊大府，光昭盛化。

translations.literal: 'He should assist in clarifying policy and seasoning the great cauldron, supporting the chief minister and spreading enlightened rule.'
translations.idiomatic: He belonged at court harmonizing institutions and magnifying the minister's work.

sentences.zh: 非徒子奇、甘羅之儔，兼包顏、冉、游、夏之美。

translations.literal: 'He is not merely another Ziqi or Gan Luo; he combines the virtues of Yan, Ran, You, and Xia.'
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was told to expect not a mere boy wonder but someone rivaling Confucius's finest disciples.

sentences.zh: 」爽乃辟為掾，襲父爵清陽亭侯，遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Shuang therefore summoned him as an aide; Xiu inherited his father's Qingyang village marquisate and was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang took him on staff; Xiu succeeded to the Qingyang village fief and entered the palace corps.

sentences.zh: 爽誅，以故吏免。

translations.literal: When Shuang was executed, Xiu lost office as a former subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang's fall stripped Xiu of rank as an affiliated official.

sentences.zh: 頃之，為廷尉正，曆文帝安東及衛將軍司馬，軍國之政，多見信納。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he became Director of Justice of the Court of Trials and successively Major under Emperor Wen's General of the East and General of the Guard; military and civil plans often followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: He soon judged cases at court, then advised Sima Zhao as army major through the eastern and household commands, shaping both strategy and administration.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supernumerary Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to supernumerary palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝之討諸葛誕也，秀與尚書僕射陳泰、黃門侍郎鍾會以行台從，豫參謀略。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Zhuge Dan, Xiu accompanied Minister of the Left Chen Tai and Palace Attendant Zhong Hui with the mobile headquarters staff and took part in strategic planning.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhuge Dan campaign he rode with Chen Tai and Zhong Hui on the field headquarters staff, shaping operational plans.

sentences.zh: 及誕平，轉尚書，進封魯陽鄉侯，增邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Dan was suppressed, Xiu was transferred to Director of the Department of State Affairs, advanced to Marquis of the Luyang district, with an additional thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's defeat brought him the ministry, a Luyang district marquisate, and a thousand extra households.

sentences.zh: 常道鄉公立，以豫議定策，進爵縣侯，增邑七百戶，遷尚書僕射。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Changdao was enthroned, Xiu shared in the preliminary council that fixed the succession; he was advanced to county marquis with seven hundred more households and promoted to Minister of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He helped seat the Duke of Changdao and earned a county marquisate, seven hundred added households, and the ministry of the left.

sentences.zh: 魏咸熙初，厘革憲司。

translations.literal: In the early Wei Xianxi era the statutory offices were overhauled.
translations.idiomatic: Wei reform reached the legal organs in the first Xianxi years.

sentences.zh: 時荀顗定禮儀，賈充正法律，而秀改官制焉。

translations.literal: Xun Yi fixed ritual; Jia Chong corrected statutes; Xiu redesigned official ranks.
translations.idiomatic: While Xun Yi handled rites and Jia Chong the code, Xiu rewrote the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 秀議五等之爵，自騎督已上六百餘人皆封。

translations.literal: Xiu proposed the five ranks of nobility; more than six hundred men from Cavalry Commander upward received fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: His scheme of five noble grades ennobled over six hundred officers from cavalry commander up.

sentences.zh: 於是秀封濟川侯，地方六十里，邑千四百戶，以高苑縣濟川墟為侯國。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jichuan, with a territory sixty li square and 1,400 households, making the Jichuan canton of Gaoyuan county his marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: He himself became marquis of Jichuan—sixty square li and fourteen hundred households centered on the Gaoyuan canton.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝未定嗣，而屬意舞陽侯攸。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Wen had not settled on an heir and favored the Marquis of Wuyang, Sima You.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao still hesitated over the succession, his eye rested on Prince You of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 武帝懼不得立，問秀曰：「人有相否？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu—then heir apparent—feared being passed over and asked Xiu, 'Can faces reveal destiny?'
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince Sima Yan feared exclusion and asked whether physiognomy foretold fate.

sentences.zh: 」因以奇表示之。

translations.literal: He then displayed his extraordinary appearance.
translations.idiomatic: He unveiled his own striking features for Xiu to read.

sentences.zh: 秀後言于文帝曰：「中撫軍人望既茂，天表如此，固非人臣之相也。

translations.literal: Xiu later told Emperor Wen, 'The General Who Guards the Center commands overwhelming esteem, and his august bearing is not the aspect of a mere subject.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiu later assured Sima Zhao that Sima Yan's commanding presence marked him for more than ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 」由是世子乃定。

translations.literal: Thereby the heir-apparent was settled.
translations.idiomatic: That endorsement fixed Yan as heir.

sentences.zh: 武帝既即王位，拜尚書令、右光祿大夫，與御史大夫王沈、衛將軍賈充俱開府，加給事中。

translations.literal: Once Emperor Wu assumed the princely throne, Xiu became Director of the Department of State Affairs and Right Imperial Household Grandee; like Wang Shen and Jia Chong he kept an independent headquarters and took palace bureau duties.
translations.idiomatic: As Prince of Jin, Yan named Xiu minister of state and right household grandee alongside Wang Shen and Jia Chong, each with separate offices and palace portfolios.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，加左光祿大夫，封钜鹿郡公，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, Xiu added the title Left Imperial Household Grandee and was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu commandery with three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jin founding Xiu gained the left household grandee, the Julu ducal fief, and three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 時安遠護軍郝詡與故人書云：「與尚書令裴秀相知，望其為益。

translations.literal: At the time the Protector Hao Xu wrote an old acquaintance, 'I know Director Pei Xiu well and hope he will aid me.'
translations.idiomatic: Protector Hao Xu boasted of pull with Minister Pei in a private letter.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏免秀官，詔曰：「不能使人之不加諸我，此古人所難。

translations.literal: The authorities memorialized to dismiss Xiu, but an edict said, 'That others should not impose wrongs upon oneself—the ancients deemed this difficult.'
translations.idiomatic: Censors indicted Xiu, yet the throne quoted the classical maxim that no ruler can stop others from gossiping.

sentences.zh: 交關人事，詡之罪耳，豈尚書令能防乎！

translations.literal: 'To intrigue among men is Xu's crime; how could the Director of the Department of Affairs prevent it!'
translations.idiomatic: Court intrigue was Xu's fault, not Pei's,

sentences.zh: 其勿有所問。

translations.literal: 'Let there be no inquiry.'
translations.idiomatic: the edict concluded, dismissing charges.

sentences.zh: 」司隸校尉李憙復上言，騎都尉劉尚為尚書令裴秀占官稻田，求禁止秀。

translations.literal: The Colonel Director of Retainers Li Xi submitted again: Commandant of Cavalry Liu Shang had seized official rice paddies on behalf of Minister Pei Xiu, and he asked that Xiu be restricted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi then accused Liu Shang of grabbing state grain fields for Pei and demanded Pei's house arrest.

sentences.zh: 詔又以秀幹翼朝政，有勳績於王室，不可以小疵掩大德，使推正尚罪而解秀禁止焉。

translations.literal: Another edict answered that Xiu upheld the government and had served the royal house with merit; small faults must not eclipse great virtue—have Shang prosecuted and lift Xiu's restriction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused: Pei's stewardship outweighed petty corruption; punish Shang instead and release Pei.

sentences.zh: 久之，詔曰：「夫三司之任，以翼宣皇極，弼成王事者也。

translations.literal: After some time an edict declared: 'The Three Dukes exist to support the supreme pivot and complete the king's work.'
translations.idiomatic: Months later a pronouncement framed the three highest ministers as pillars of the throne.

sentences.zh: 故經國論道，賴之明喆，苟非其人，官不虛備。

translations.literal: 'Therefore ordering the realm and debating the Way depends on enlightened men; ill-suited officers must not fill honored posts in vain.'
translations.idiomatic: Good government requires worthy occupants; hollow titles dishonor the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、左光祿大夫裴秀，雅量弘博，思心通遠，先帝登庸，贊事前朝。

translations.literal: 'Director of the Department of State Affairs and Left Imperial Household Grandee Pei Xiu combines generous breadth with searching thought; the late emperor raised him to advance the former court.'
translations.idiomatic: It singled out Pei—minister of state and left household grandee—for wisdom cultivated under the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 朕受明命，光佐大業，勳德茂著，配蹤元凱。

translations.literal: 'I have received the luminous mandate; he brilliantly assists the great enterprise; merit and virtue flourish and match the deeds of Yuan and Kai.'
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor hailed Pei's aid as rivaling the ancient worthies Gaoyuan and Kai.

sentences.zh: 宜正位居體，以康庶績。

translations.literal: He ought to occupy the proper station and conform his person so as to bring tranquility to the manifold tasks.
translations.idiomatic: He should assume the fitting office and embody his role so that every branch of government thrives.

sentences.zh: 其以秀為司空。」

translations.literal: Let Pei Xiu be appointed Minister of Works."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint Pei Xiu Minister of Works."

sentences.zh: 秀儒學洽聞，且留心政事，當禪代之際，總納言之要，其所裁當，禮無違者。

translations.literal: Xiu was steeped in Confucian learning and broadly informed, and he attended closely to government; during the abdication transition he held the portfolio that gathers memorials and voices policy, and whatever he ruled on matched ritual without breach.
translations.idiomatic: Trained in the classics and widely read, Xiu focused on administration; at the dynastic handover he controlled the channels of counsel, and his rulings never violated prescribed ritual.

sentences.zh: 又以職在地官，以《禹貢》山川地名，從來久遠，多有變易。

translations.literal: Moreover, because his portfolio belonged to the Ministry of Earth, the mountains, rivers, and place names recorded in the "Tribute of Yu" had, across long ages, undergone many alterations.
translations.idiomatic: His duties under the earth ministry also concerned the "Tribute of Yu," whose topography had shifted across centuries.

sentences.zh: 後世說者或強牽引，漸以暗昧。

translations.literal: Later commentators sometimes forced strained glosses, and understanding grew murky.
translations.idiomatic: Later exegetes often forced contrived readings, obscuring the original geography.

sentences.zh: 於是甄摘舊文，疑者則闕，古有名而今無者，皆隨事注列，作《禹貢地域圖》十八篇，奏之，藏于秘府。

translations.literal: Thereupon he culled the old text, leaving blanks wherever doubtful; wherever an ancient name survived but no modern one existed, he annotated each case in order, composed the eighteen-scroll "Regional Map of the Tribute of Yu," presented it, and deposited it in the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: He sifted the classical text, omitted uncertain points, glossed every obsolete toponym, and submitted his eighteen-scroll "Yugong" atlas to the palace library.

sentences.zh: 其序曰：

translations.literal: Its preface states:
translations.idiomatic: The preface begins:

sentences.zh: 秀創制朝儀，廣陳刑政，朝廷多遵用之，以為故事。

translations.literal: Xiu framed court ceremonies and expounded penal administration; the court largely adopted his models as standing precedent.
translations.idiomatic: His protocols for audience and criminal policy became the templates the court routinely followed.

sentences.zh: 在位四載，為當世名公。

translations.literal: During four years in office he ranked among the celebrated ministers of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Across four years at court he stood among the reign's most eminent statesmen.

sentences.zh: 服寒食散，當飲熱酒而飲冷酒，泰始七年薨，時年四十八。

translations.literal: He took cold-food powder, which required warm wine, yet drank cold; in the seventh year of Taishi he died, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Abusing the cold-food elixir with chilled wine instead of warm killed him in Taishi year seven at forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「司空經德履哲，體蹈儒雅，佐命翼世，勳業弘茂。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The Minister of Works treads virtue and embraces wisdom; his person embodies Confucian refinement; he aided the Mandate and sustained the age; his merit and enterprise are vast."
translations.idiomatic: The throne mourned: "The minister embodied learning and wisdom, shaped the founding enterprise, and built vast achievements."

sentences.zh: 方將宣獻敷制，為世宗範，不幸薨殂，朕甚痛之。

translations.literal: "We had hoped he would proclaim models and spread regulations, to be an exemplar for generations; unluckily he has expired, and We are deeply stricken."
translations.idiomatic: "We expected fresh institutions from him; his death leaves us grief-stricken."

sentences.zh: 其賜秘器、朝服一具、衣一襲、錢三十萬、布百匹。

translations.literal: Let him be granted mortuary regalia, one full court robe, one suit of clothes, three hundred thousand cash, and one hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The burial grant included ritual vessels, court dress, a full wardrobe, three hundred thousand coins, and a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 諡曰元。」

translations.literal: His posthumous title shall be Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he received the epithet Yuan."

sentences.zh: 初，秀以尚書三十六曹統事准例不明，宜使諸卿任職，未及奏而薨。

translations.literal: At first Xiu had held that the thirty-six bureaus of the Department of State Affairs followed unclear precedents and that the chief ministers ought each to bear real duties; before he could memorialize, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He had planned to clarify the thirty-six directorates and devolve power to senior ministers but died before submitting the reform.

sentences.zh: 其友人料其書記，得表草言平吳之事，其詞曰：「孫皓酷虐，不及聖明禦世兼弱攻昧，使遺子孫，將遂不能臣；

translations.literal: His friends sorted his papers and found a draft memorial on pacifying Wu; its wording read: "Sun Hao is cruel and violent; he cannot match a sage ruler who governs the age, annexes the weak, and attacks the benighted—if we leave his line heirs on the throne, our descendants will never be able to serve him as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Editors recovered his Wu campaign draft: Sun Hao's cruelty could not compare with a true sage who annexes weak states and strikes dull rulers—leave him an heir, it warned, and future Jin ministers could not long bow to Wu.

sentences.zh: 時有否泰，非萬安之勢也。

translations.literal: The times have their seasons of peace and peril; this is not a posture of perfect security.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunes rise and fall; no dynasty rests eternally secure.

sentences.zh: 臣昔雖已屢言，未有成旨。

translations.literal: Your servant has spoken repeatedly yet never received a decisive reply.
translations.idiomatic: Though I have urged this often, no firm answer came.

sentences.zh: 今既疾篤不起，謹重屍啟。

translations.literal: Now that my illness is desperate and I cannot rise, I respectfully submit this plea from one already as good as dead.
translations.idiomatic: On my deathbed I press the matter once more.

sentences.zh: 願陛下時共施用。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will adopt it in concert with other measures without delay.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to enact it alongside companion policies at once.

sentences.zh: 」乃封以上聞。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they sealed the draft and forwarded it.
translations.idiomatic: They forwarded the sealed memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「司空薨，痛悼不能去心。

translations.literal: An edict replied: "The Minister of Works has died; Our grief cannot leave Our heart."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered: "We cannot shake our sorrow at losing the minister."

sentences.zh: 又得表草，雖在危困，不忘王室，盡忠憂國。

translations.literal: "Moreover We have obtained the draft memorial; though in mortal danger, he did not forget the royal house and exhausted loyalty in worrying for the state."
translations.idiomatic: "His draft shows that even dying he thought only of the dynasty's welfare."

sentences.zh: 省益傷切，輒當與諸賢共論也。」

translations.literal: "Reading it deepens Our wounded grief; We shall discuss it at once with the worthies."
translations.idiomatic: "Its words wound us anew; we will take counsel with the ministers immediately."

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，與石苞等並為王公，配享廟庭。

translations.literal: In the early Xianning era he received paired sacrifice in the ancestral temple alongside Shi Bao and others among the highest nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning he joined Shi Bao and other peers as a spirit recipient in the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 有二子：浚、頠。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Jun and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Pei Jun and Pei Yi.

sentences.zh: 浚嗣位，至散騎常侍，早卒。

translations.literal: Jun succeeded to the title; he reached Supernumerary Palace Attendant and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Jun inherited the fief, rose to supernumerary attendant, and died young.

sentences.zh: 浚庶子憬不惠，別封高陽亭侯，以浚少弟頠嗣。

translations.literal: Jun's bastard son Jing was dull-witted; Jing was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of the Gaoyang village, and Jun's younger brother Yi succeeded to the main line.
translations.idiomatic: The dull illegitimate Jing received a minor Gaoyang village marquisate while the legitimate junior uncle Yi took the primary succession.

translations.literal: The received text gives a lone equals sign between subsections.
translations.idiomatic: The manuscript inserts an equals sign here as a sectional marker.

sentences.zh: 子頠

translations.literal: Yi
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi

sentences.zh: =頠字逸民。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Yimin.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi, whose courtesy name was Yimin,

sentences.zh: 弘雅有遠識，博學稽古，自少知名。

translations.literal: He was magnanimous and refined, with far-reaching insight; broadly learned and versed in antiquity, he was renowned from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned while still young, he combined Classical breadth with long vision.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞周弼見而歎曰：「頠若武庫，五兵縱橫，一時之傑也。

translations.literal: The Palace Assistant Censor Zhou Bi saw him and sighed: "Yi is like an arsenal—every sort of weapon deployed at once—the outstanding man of the hour."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bi likened him to an armory bristling with arms—a singular talent.

sentences.zh: 」賈充即頠從母夫也，表「秀有佐命之勳，不幸嫡長喪亡，遺孤稚弱。

translations.literal: " Jia Chong was Yi's uncle by marriage; he memorialized: "Pei Xiu performed merit founding the dynasty; unluckily his eldest legitimate son died young, leaving a feeble orphan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong—Yi's uncle-in-law—argued that Xiu's founding honors deserved an heir, yet the legitimate eldest had died, leaving a helpless child.

sentences.zh: 頠才德英茂，足以興隆國嗣。

translations.literal: Yi's talent and virtue are splendid—more than adequate to renew the successor line of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yi boasted virtue enough to sustain the ducal succession.

sentences.zh: 」詔頠襲爵，頠固讓，不許。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered Yi to inherit the noble rank; Yi firmly declined but permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Yi to succeed; he refused repeatedly yet had to accept.

sentences.zh: 太康二年，徵為太子中庶子，遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taikang he was summoned as Palace Mentor to the heir apparent and promoted to Supernumerary Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang year two brought him tutor of the heir and promotion to supernumerary attendant.

sentences.zh: 惠帝既位，轉國子祭酒，兼右軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui assumed the throne, Yi was transferred to Libationer of the Imperial Academy while retaining concurrent appointment as General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui he directed the imperial academy and still led the right guard.

sentences.zh: 初，頠兄子憬為白衣，頠論述世勳，賜爵高陽亭侯。

translations.literal: At first Yi's nephew Jing was a commoner in white; Yi expounded the family's generations of merit, and Jing was granted the noble rank of Marquis of the Gaoyang village.
translations.idiomatic: Once cousin Jing wore only commoner's garb, Yi narrated the clan's achievements until the court ennobled Jing at Gaoyang village.

sentences.zh: 楊駿將誅也，駿党左軍將軍劉豫陳兵在門，遇頠，問太傅所在。

translations.literal: When Yang Jun was about to be executed, Jun's partisan General of the Left Army Liu Yu deployed troops at the gate; he met Yi and asked where the Grand Tutor was.
translations.idiomatic: As Yang Jun fell, Liu Yu—Jun's colonel of the left—blocked the gate and demanded Sima Liang's whereabouts.

sentences.zh: 頠紿之曰：「向於西掖門遇公乘素車，從二人西出矣。

translations.literal: Yi deceived him: "Just now at the Western Portal I met the Duke riding in an unadorned carriage with two followers heading west."
translations.idiomatic: Yi lied that he had seen the grand tutor leave west through the western portal in a plain cart.

sentences.zh: 」豫曰：「吾何之？

translations.literal: " Yu said, "Where shall I go?"
translations.idiomatic: "Where should I run?" Yu asked.

sentences.zh: 」頠曰：「宜至廷尉。

translations.literal: " Yi said, "You ought to report to the Minister of Justice."
translations.idiomatic: "Surrender to the Ministry of Justice," Yi replied.

sentences.zh: 」豫從頠言，遂委而去。

translations.literal: " Yu followed Yi's words, threw down his arms, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu obeyed, abandoned his post, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尋而詔頠代豫領左軍將軍，屯萬春門。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered Yi to replace Yu and command the Left Army, stationed at Wanchun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yi soon replaced Yu as colonel of the left, camped at Wanchun Gate.

sentences.zh: 及駿誅，以功當封武昌侯，頠請以封憬，帝竟封頠次子該。

translations.literal: When Jun was executed, Yi merited enfeoffment as Marquis of Wuchang for service; Yi requested the title for Jing, but the emperor in the end enfeoffed Yi's second son Gai.
translations.idiomatic: After Jun's purge Yi earned a Wuchang marquisate but begged to transfer it to Jing; the throne instead ennobled second son Gai.

sentences.zh: 頠苦陳憬本承嫡，宜襲钜鹿，先帝恩旨，辭不獲命。

translations.literal: Yi bitterly argued that Jing, as heir designate, ought to inherit Julu under the late emperor's decree—he declined but could not escape the command.
translations.idiomatic: Yi insisted Jing deserved the Julu title per the late emperor's grace yet could not refuse the earlier mandate.

sentences.zh: 武昌之封，己之所蒙，特請以封憬。

translations.literal: The Wuchang honor was what he himself had received; he specially requested it be transferred to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to give his own Wuchang prize to Jing.

sentences.zh: 該時尚主，故帝不聽。

translations.literal: Gai had by then married a princess, so the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gai had married into the imperial clan, the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍中。

translations.literal: Yi was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose again to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 時天下暫寧，頠奏修國學，刻石寫經。

translations.literal: When the realm was briefly at peace, Yi memorialized to restore the imperial academy and carve the classics on stone.
translations.idiomatic: During the lull he urged rebuilding the academy and cutting stone classics.

sentences.zh: 皇太子既講，釋奠祀孔子，飲饗射侯，甚有儀序。

translations.literal: After the crown prince had lectured, they performed the grain-offering to Confucius, feasted, and held archery contests—the observances were well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Once the heir finished lectures, courtiers sacrificed to Confucius, banqueted, and shot at targets with punctilious ritual.

sentences.zh: 又令荀籓終父勖之志，鑄鐘鑿磬，以備郊廟朝享禮樂。

translations.literal: He also had Xun Fan fulfill his father Xun Xu's intent, casting bells and chiseling chimes to supply suburban sacrifices, temple offerings, and court music.
translations.idiomatic: He tasked Xun Fan with casting bells and lithophones for suburban rites and ancestral music, honoring Xun Xu's unfinished plan.

sentences.zh: 頠通博多聞，兼明醫術。

translations.literal: Yi was broadly learned and well informed, and also understood medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Besides encyclopedic scholarship he practiced medicine.

sentences.zh: 荀勖之修律度也，檢得古尺，短世所用四分有餘。

translations.literal: When Xun Xiu revised pitch pipes and measures, inspection recovered an ancient foot shorter than those in current use by more than one fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu's pitch reform uncovered an old foot-rule nearly a quarter shorter than contemporary measures.

sentences.zh: 頠上言：「宜改諸度量。

translations.literal: Yi submitted: "All weights and measures ought to be changed.
translations.idiomatic: "Every balance and yardstick needs reform," he wrote.

sentences.zh: 若未能悉革，可先改太醫權衡。

translations.literal: If they cannot all be reformed at once, begin by changing the scales for the Imperial Pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: If wholesale change is impossible, start with the imperial dispensary's weights.

sentences.zh: 此若差違，遂失神農、岐伯之正。

translations.literal: If these miss the standard, one loses the correct measures of Shennong and Qi Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Wrong measures betray Shennong and Qi Bo's pharmacological norms.

sentences.zh: 藥物輕重，分兩乖互，所可傷夭，為害尤深。

translations.literal: When drugs vary in weight and portions contradict each other, the harm to life can be especially grave.
translations.idiomatic: Inconsistent dosages kill patients.

sentences.zh: 古壽考而今短折者，未必不由此也。

translations.literal: That antiquity enjoyed long life while today people die young is not necessarily unrelated to this."
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps shorter modern lifespans stem from exactly these errors."

sentences.zh: 」卒不能用。

translations.literal: " In the end [his advice] was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court ignored him.

sentences.zh: 樂廣嘗與頠清言，欲以理服之，而頠辭論豐博，廣笑而不言。

translations.literal: Yue Guang once engaged Yi in pure conversation, intending to prevail by logic, but Yi's discourse was rich and ample; Guang smiled and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Guang tried to win a xuanxue debate yet yielded silently before Yi's torrent.

sentences.zh: 時人謂頠為言談之林藪。

translations.literal: People of the time called Yi the forest and marsh of conversation.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries dubbed him the wilderness where discourse gathered.

sentences.zh: 頠以賈后不悅太子，抗表請增崇太子所生謝淑妃位號，仍啟增置後衛率吏，給三千兵，於是東宮宿衛萬人。

translations.literal: Because Empress Jia disliked the crown prince, Yi submitted a blunt memorial asking to elevate the rank title of Consort Xie who bore the heir, and further requested adding rear-guard officers for the heir's household with three thousand troops—thereupon the Eastern Palace had ten thousand household guards overnight.
translations.idiomatic: To shield Crown Prince Yu against Empress Jia's spite, Yi demanded higher honors for Lady Xie and three thousand extra rear-guard troops, swelling the heir's garrison to ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書，侍中如故，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Department of State Affairs, kept Palace Attendant as before, with additional title Household Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He moved up to minister of state, kept his attendant post, and gained the household grandee title.

sentences.zh: 每授一職，未嘗不殷勤固讓，表疏十餘上，博引古今成敗以為言，覽之者莫不寒心。

translations.literal: Each time he received an appointment he invariably declined earnestly; his memorials ran to more than ten submissions, citing successes and failures from antiquity to the present—those who read them felt chill in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Every promotion drew stacks of refusal memorials stuffed with historical warnings that chilled every reader.

sentences.zh: 頠深慮賈后亂政，與司空張華、侍中賈模議廢之而立謝淑妃。

translations.literal: Yi deeply feared Empress Jia would disorder the government; together with Minister of Works Zhang Hua and Palace Attendant Jia Mo he discussed deposing her and enthroning Consort Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Jia Nanfeng's misrule, he plotted with Zhang Hua and Jia Mo to replace her with Lady Xie.

sentences.zh: 華、模皆曰：「帝自無廢黜之意，若吾等專行之，上心不以為是。

translations.literal: Hua and Mo both said: "The emperor himself has no intent to dismiss her; if we act alone in this, in his heart he will not approve.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor never meant to depose her," Zhang and Jia replied; acting alone would anger him.

sentences.zh: 且諸王方剛，朋黨異議，恐禍如發機，身死國危，無益社稷。

translations.literal: Moreover the princes are just now forceful; factions argue differently—we fear disaster would strike like a spring-trigger—our deaths and the state's peril would benefit the altars not at all.
translations.idiomatic: The martial princes split into factions; forcing the issue might spring a trap that kills us without saving the realm.

sentences.zh: 」頠曰：「誠如公慮。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "Truly it is as you fear.
translations.idiomatic: "True enough," Yi conceded.

sentences.zh: 但昏虐之人，無所忌憚，亂可立待，將如之何？

translations.literal: Yet a benighted and cruel person fears nothing; chaos can arrive at once—what then are we to do?"
translations.idiomatic: "Yet a reckless tyrant invites instant chaos—what then?"

sentences.zh: 」華曰：「卿二人猶且見信，然勤為左右陳禍福之戒，冀無大悖。

translations.literal: " Hua said: "You two are still trusted; diligently instruct him left and right on the consequences of fortune and disaster, and perhaps there will be no great rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: "Stay close and lecture him on fortune and ruin," Zhang urged.

sentences.zh: 幸天下尚安，庶可優遊卒歲。

translations.literal: Fortunately the realm is still calm; perhaps we can drift through our years."
translations.idiomatic: "While peace lasts we might survive."

sentences.zh: 」此謀遂寢。

translations.literal: " This plan then was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: They dropped the plot.

sentences.zh: 頠旦夕勸說從母廣城君，令戒喻賈后親待太子而已。

translations.literal: Morning and evening Yi urged his maternal aunt the Lady of Guangcheng to instruct Empress Jia to cherish the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yi besought Aunt Guangcheng daily to teach Nanfeng to honor the heir.

sentences.zh: 或說頠曰：「幸與中宮內外可得盡言。

translations.literal: Someone said to Yi: "Fortunately you have full access inside and outside the palace—speak exhaustively.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers told him he alone could speak freely across palace walls.

sentences.zh: 言若不行，則可辭病摒退。

translations.literal: If your words do not prevail, you may plead illness and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: If ignored, resign on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 若二者不立，雖有十表，難乎免矣。

translations.literal: If neither course can be established, though you submit ten memorials, escape will be hard."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise ten memorials will not spare you."

sentences.zh: 」頠慨然久之，而竟不能行。

translations.literal: " Yi sighed deeply for a long time but in the end could not act.
translations.idiomatic: Yi brooded yet never acted.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左僕射，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Senior Minister of the Left of the Department of State Affairs, Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He became senior minister of the left while remaining attendant.

sentences.zh: 頠雖後之親屬，然雅望素隆，四海不謂之以親戚進也，惟恐其不居位。

translations.literal: Though Yi was kin to the empress, his lofty reputation had long stood—none under heaven thought he had risen through kinship; they only feared he might leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Despite ties to Nanfeng, his prestige rested on merit; the realm dreaded losing him, not nepotism.

sentences.zh: 俄復使頠專任門下事，固讓，不聽。

translations.literal: Soon he was again assigned sole charge of Chancellery affairs; he firmly declined and was not heard.
translations.idiomatic: The court tried to leave the entire Chancellery to him; refusals went unheard.

sentences.zh: 頠上言：「賈模適亡，復以臣代，崇外戚之望，彰偏私之舉。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized: "Jia Mo has just died; again substituting me increases expectation toward outside kin and displays partial favor.
translations.idiomatic: "Replacing Jia Mo with me," he warned, "spotlights consort power."

sentences.zh: 後族何常有能自保，皆知重親無脫者也。

translations.literal: When has a maternal clan ever been able to protect itself? All know that leaning on kinship brings no escape.
translations.idiomatic: No maternal house survives forever by leaning on blood ties.

sentences.zh: 然漢二十四帝惟孝文、光武、明帝不重外戚，皆保其宗，豈將獨賢，實以安理故也。

translations.literal: Yet among the twenty-four Han emperors only Wen, Guangwu, and Ming did not favor maternal relatives—all preserved their houses; were they uniquely worthy? Truly they acted by principles that kept peace.
translations.idiomatic: Only Han Wen, Guangwu, and Ming avoided nepotism—and kept their dynasties secure.

sentences.zh: 昔穆叔不拜越禮之饗，臣亦不敢聞殊常之詔。

translations.literal: Once Uncle Mu declined a feast that breached ritual; your servant too does not dare hear an extraordinary edict."
translations.idiomatic: Like Shu Zhao rejecting improper feasts, I cannot obey irregular favors."

sentences.zh: 」又表云：「咎繇謨虞，伊尹相商，呂望翊周，蕭張佐漢，咸播功化，光格四極。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Gao Yao planned for Yu, Yi Yin aided Shang, Lü Wang assisted Zhou, Xiao He and Zhang Liang aided Han—all spread merit and transformation and their brilliance reached the four poles.
translations.idiomatic: His second essay cited Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Lü Wang, Xiao He, and Zhang Liang as ministers whose virtue illumined the corners of the world.

sentences.zh: 暨于繼體，咎單、傅說，祖己、樊仲，亦隆中興。

translations.literal: At the succession of heirs, Gu Dan, Fu Yue, Zu Yi, Fan Zhong likewise prospered mid-restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser heirs too relied on Gu Dan, Fu Yue, Zu Yi, and Fan Zhong during revivals.

sentences.zh: 或明揚側陋，或起自庶族，豈非尚德之舉，以臻斯美哉！

translations.literal: Some were promoted from humble obscurity, some rose from common clans—were these not deeds that honored virtue and attained such beauty!
translations.idiomatic: Elevating talent over pedigree produced golden ages.

sentences.zh: 曆觀近世，不能慕遠，溺於近情，多任後親，以致不靜。

translations.literal: Looking over recent ages, rulers could not emulate antiquity and drowned in private feeling; most entrusted maternal kin, hence unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Later courts chased sentiment and stuffed offices with in-laws—hence chaos.

sentences.zh: 昔疏廣戒太子以舅氏為官屬，前世以為知禮。

translations.literal: Once Shu Guang warned the crown prince against taking maternal uncles as household officers—the former age deemed that knowing ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Guang once forbade crown-prince posts for maternal uncles—praised as ritual correctness.

sentences.zh: 況朝廷何取于外戚，正復才均，尚當先其疏者，以明至公。

translations.literal: How much less should the court favor maternal relatives—when talents are even, one ought still to prefer the more distant, to manifest utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Even when talent matches, prefer distant kin to prove impartiality.

sentences.zh: 漢世不用馮野王，即其事也。

translations.literal: The Han never employed Feng Yewang—that exemplifies the point.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi refused Feng Yewang for just that lesson.

sentences.zh: 」表上，皆優詔敦譬。

translations.literal: When the memorials went up, each received kindly edicts urging him to yield.
translations.idiomatic: Each memorial drew soothing replies begging him to stay.

sentences.zh: 時以陳准子匡、韓蔚子嵩並侍東宮，頠諫曰：「東宮之建，以儲皇極。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Zhun's son Kuang and Han Wei's son Song both attended the Eastern Palace; Yi remonstrated: "The Eastern Palace exists to store the supreme pivot.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Kuang and Han Song waited on the heir, Yi protested that the Eastern Palace anchors the throne.

sentences.zh: 其所與遊接，必簡英俊，宜用成德。

translations.literal: Those who lodge and associate there must be chosen from the talented and heroic; men of completed virtue should serve.
translations.idiomatic: Its companions must be seasoned worthies.

sentences.zh: 匡、嵩幼弱，未識人理立身之節。

translations.literal: Kuang and Song are young and weak and do not grasp the norms of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang and Song were mere boys ignorant of duty.

sentences.zh: 東宮實體夙成之表，而今有童子侍從之聲，未是光闡遐風之弘理也。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace ought to display maturity; yet now there is the reputation of boys attending—the principles for broadcasting distant virtue are not thereby clarified."
translations.idiomatic: Stationing children there signals boy-emperor gossip, hardly an august tutorial vision.

sentences.zh: 」湣懷太子之廢也，頠與張華苦爭不從，語在《華傳》。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai was deposed, Yi with Zhang Hua bitterly disputed but was not heeded—the account is in Hua's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Zhang Hua fought bitterly against Minhuai's removal—the fuller story sits in Zhang's biography.

sentences.zh: 頠深患時俗放蕩，不尊儒術，何晏、阮籍素有高名於世，口談浮虛，不遵禮法，屍祿耽寵，仕不事事；

translations.literal: Yi deeply worried that the customs of the age were unrestrained and did not honor Confucian teaching; He Yan and Ruan Ji enjoyed lofty reputations in the world, talking idle emptiness at the mouth and not observing ritual law—drawing salary and indulging favor while holding office yet doing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi despised how fashion praised He Yan and Ruan Ji for idle chatter that ignored ritual while they pocketed salaries and neglected duty.

sentences.zh: 至王衍之徒，聲譽太盛，位高勢重，不以物務自嬰，遂相放效，風教陵遲，乃著崇有之論以釋其蔽曰：

translations.literal: When it came to Wang Yan and his sort, their reputations swelled too large; occupying high rank and heavy power, they refused to burden themselves with concrete duties, whereupon others copied them in turn—moral instruction slid downhill—so Yi drafted his discourse "Exalting Being" to expose that sickness, saying:
translations.idiomatic: By Wang Yan's generation fame had inflated, office brought lazy emulation, and teaching collapsed—Yi answered with his "Exalting Being" essay to cure the cult of emptiness.

sentences.zh: 王衍之徒攻難交至，並莫能屈。

translations.literal: Wang Yan's clique besieged him with objections, yet none could break his argument.
translations.idiomatic: The qingtan circle attacked his thesis from every side without refuting it.

sentences.zh: 又著《辯才論》，古今精義皆辨釋焉，未成而遇禍。

translations.literal: He also composed the "Treatise on Eloquence," clarifying every subtle point ancient and modern; he did not finish it before catastrophe struck.
translations.idiomatic: His unfinished "Treatise on Eloquence" surveyed classical debates but death cut it short.

sentences.zh: 初，趙王倫諂事賈后，頠甚惡之，倫數求官，頠與張華復固執不許，由是深為倫所怨。

translations.literal: At first the Prince of Zhao, Sima Lun, fawned on Empress Jia; Yi loathed him. Lun repeatedly sought promotion; Yi and Zhang Hua steadfastly refused—thereby earning Lun's bitter hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun curried Jia Nanfeng's favor while Yi and Zhang Hua blocked his offices, planting a deadly grudge.

sentences.zh: 倫又潛懷篡逆，欲先除朝望，因廢賈后之際遂誅之，時年三十四。

translations.literal: Lun also nursed usurpation: wishing first to eliminate eminent ministers, he executed Yi while deposing the empress; Yi was thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Lun used Jia's fall as cover to murder Yi at thirty-four while plotting a coup.

sentences.zh: 二子嵩、該，倫亦欲害之。

translations.literal: His sons Song and Gai—Lun meant to kill them too.
translations.idiomatic: Lun targeted Yi's sons Song and Gai next.

sentences.zh: 梁王肜、東海王越稱頠父秀有勳王室，配食太廟，不宜滅其後嗣，故得不死，徙帶方；

translations.literal: Princes Sima Yong of Liang and Sima Yue of Donghai declared that Yi's father Xiu had served the dynasty and received offerings in the Grand Temple—his line must not be extinguished—so the boys lived on, banished to Daifang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Donghai princes cited Xiu's temple honors to spare the sons, exiling them to Liaodong instead.

sentences.zh: 惠帝反正，追復頠本官，改葬以卿禮，諡曰成。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui was restored, Yi's offices were posthumously reinstated; he was reburied with ministerial ceremony and titled Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui's restoration Yi won reinstatement, a proper reburial, and the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 以嵩嗣爵，為中書黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Song inherited the title and became palace attendant and palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The marquisate passed to Song in the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 該出後從伯凱，為散騎常侍，並為乞活賊陳午所害。

translations.literal: Gai had been posthumously adopted to uncle Kai; he was supernumerary attendant until both brothers fell to Chen Wu's Qi Huo band.
translations.idiomatic: Adopted heir Gai died beside Song when Chen Wu's refugee warriors slaughtered them.

translations.literal: The received text gives a lone equals sign between subsections.
translations.idiomatic: An equals sign marks the break before Pei Kai's biography.

sentences.zh: 秀從弟楷

translations.literal: Pei Kai, Xiu's younger cousin
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kai—cousin to Pei Xiu

sentences.zh: =楷字叔則。

translations.literal: Kai, courtesy name Shuzé.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kai, whose courtesy name was Shuzé,

sentences.zh: 父徽，魏冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Wei had been Governor of Jizhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Father Pei Wei governed Ji province for Wei.

sentences.zh: 楷明悟有識量，弱冠知名，尤精《老》、《易》，少與王戎齊名。

translations.literal: Kai was lucid and discerning, with breadth of judgment; before age twenty he was famous, especially in the Laozi and Changes, and was paired in renown with Wang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Celebrated before twenty, he mastered the Daoist classics alongside Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 鍾會薦之于文帝，辟相國掾，遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui recommended him to Emperor Wen; Kai became aide to the minister of state and rose to gentleman of the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui's referral brought him into Sima Zhao's bureau and the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 賈充改定律令，以楷為定科郎。

translations.literal: When Jia Chong revised statutes, Kai served as the drafter charged with fixing each legal article.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong's law revision named Kai specialist for codifying clauses.

sentences.zh: 事畢，詔楷於御前執讀，平議當否。

translations.literal: When the code was done, an edict ordered Kai to read it aloud before the throne and debate whether each clause fit.
translations.idiomatic: At court he read the new code aloud for imperial scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 楷善宣吐，左右屬目，聽者忘倦。

translations.literal: Kai spoke with luminous clarity; attendants hung on every word and listeners forgot fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: His exposition captivated the hall.

sentences.zh: 武帝為撫軍，妙選僚采，以楷為參軍事。

translations.literal: While Emperor Wu still served as General Who Supports the Army, he chose Kai as military administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan made him staff adviser during the princely generalship.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎缺，文帝問其人於鍾會。

translations.literal: The personnel director post stood empty; Emperor Wen asked Zhong Hui whom to appoint.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao asked Zhong Hui who should head personnel.

sentences.zh: 會曰：「裴楷清通，王戎簡要，皆其選也。

translations.literal: Hui replied: "Pei Kai is lucid and penetrating; Wang Rong concise and essential—either suits the post."
translations.idiomatic: "Pei Kai or Wang Rong," said Zhong Hui, "both fit."

sentences.zh: 」於是以楷為吏部郎。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kai became Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Kai received the appointment.

sentences.zh: 楷風神高邁，容儀俊爽，博涉群書，特精理義，時人謂之「玉人」，又稱「見裴叔則如近玉山，映照人也」。

translations.literal: Kai's spirit seemed borne on the wind; his face handsome and bright; he read widely and plumbed doctrine—people called him the "jade man" and said that meeting Pei Shuzé felt like nearing a jade mountain blazing with light.
translations.idiomatic: His aura and learning earned the nickname "jade man"—seeing him was likened to climbing a luminous jade peak.

sentences.zh: 轉中書郎，出入宮省，見者肅然改容。

translations.literal: Transferred to palace secretariat gentleman, he passed through palace gates so strikingly that onlookers straightened their bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Palace corridors fell silent when he passed.

sentences.zh: 武帝初登阼，探策以卜世數多少，而得一，帝不悅，群臣失色，莫有言者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu first mounted the throne he drew oracle slips on dynastic longevity and drew "one"; the emperor frowned, ministers paled, none spoke.
translations.idiomatic: An ill-omened slip "one" from the imperial divination silenced the court.

sentences.zh: 楷正容儀，和其聲氣，從容進曰：「臣聞天得一以清，地得一以甯，王侯得一以為天下貞。

translations.literal: Kai composed his robes and moderated his tone, advanced calmly, and said: "Your servant has heard that Heaven receiving One grows clear; Earth receiving One grows still; kings and lords receiving One uphold the realm's integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kai cited the Laozi to turn one into cosmic blessing.

sentences.zh: 」武帝大悅，群臣皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu rejoiced; everyone shouted long live the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brightened and the hall cheered.

sentences.zh: 俄拜散騎侍郎，累遷散騎常侍、河內太守，入為屯騎校尉、右軍將軍，轉侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was supernumerary gentleman, then attendant, governor of Henei, colonel of household troops, general of the right guard, and palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Promotions swept him through Henei, camp command, the right guard, and back to attendant.

sentences.zh: 石崇以功臣子有才氣，與楷志趣各異，不與之交。

translations.literal: Shi Chong, proud son of a merit family, disagreed with Kai's tastes and kept his distance.
translations.idiomatic: The meritor Shi Chong avoided Kai on temperament.

sentences.zh: 長水校尉孫季舒嘗與崇酣燕，慢傲過度，崇欲表免之。

translations.literal: Colonel Sun Jishu once drank riotously with Chong, insulting others grossly; Chong planned to memorialize his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jishu's drunken arrogance at Chong's banquet nearly cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 楷聞之，謂崇曰：「足下飲人狂藥，責人正禮，不亦乖乎！

translations.literal: Kai told Chong: "You pour reckless wine yet demand ritual propriety—is that not perverse!"
translations.idiomatic: "You ply guests with reckless wine," Kai said, "then fault their manners—how absurd?"

sentences.zh: 」崇乃止。

translations.literal: Chong dropped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Chong relented.

sentences.zh: 楷性寬厚，與物無忤。

translations.literal: Kai was tolerant and magnanimous; he contended with nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Genial and conciliatory, he picked no quarrels.

sentences.zh: 不持儉素，每游榮貴，輒取其珍玩。

translations.literal: He did not affect austerity; visiting grandees he accepted their finest curios.
translations.idiomatic: He freely accepted gifts from the mighty.

sentences.zh: 雖車馬器服，宿昔之間，便以施諸窮乏。

translations.literal: Carriages, robes, vessels—overnight he gave them to the needy.
translations.idiomatic: By morning those luxuries reached the poor.

sentences.zh: 嘗營別宅，其從兄衍見而悅之，即以宅與衍。

translations.literal: He built a villa; cousin Wang Yan coveted it, so Kai gave him the house outright.
translations.idiomatic: Yan admired his new manor; Kai signed it over.

sentences.zh: 梁、趙二王，國之近屬，貴重當時，楷歲請二國租錢百萬，以散親族。

translations.literal: The Liang and Zhao princes were imperial kin of the highest rank; Kai annually took one million cash from their rents for kin.
translations.idiomatic: He diverted a million coins yearly from those princely estates to aid relatives.

sentences.zh: 人或譏之，楷曰：「損有餘以補不足，天之道也。

translations.literal: Critics sneered; Kai answered: "Taking from surplus to aid deficiency—that is Heaven's Way."
translations.idiomatic: "Redistribution follows Heaven," he replied.

sentences.zh: 」安於毀譽，其行己任率，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Untroubled by praise or blame, he lived candidly—always thus.
translations.idiomatic: He shrugged at gossip and followed instinct.

sentences.zh: 與山濤、和嶠並以盛德居位，帝嘗問曰：「朕應天順時，海內更始，天下風聲，何得何失？

translations.literal: With Shan Tao and He Jiao he governed by sheer moral weight; the emperor once asked: "We obey Heaven and renew the age—what do customs gain or lose?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu surveyed the realm's moral climate with Shan Tao and He Jiao at his side.

sentences.zh: 」楷對曰：「陛下受命，四海承風，所以未比德於堯舜者，但以賈充之徒尚在朝耳。

translations.literal: Kai replied: "Since Your Majesty received the mandate the seas embrace your wind—only men like Jia Chong still at court keep your virtue from matching Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: Kai blamed Jia Chong's lingering presence for any shortfall from sage kings.

sentences.zh: 方宜引天下賢人，與弘正道，不宜示人以私。

translations.literal: Summon worthies and enlarge the Way—do not parade private favor before the world.
translations.idiomatic: Elevate talent rather than cronies.

sentences.zh: 」時任愷、庾純亦以充為言，帝乃出充為關中都督。

translations.literal: Ren Kai and Yu Chun echoed him; the emperor posted Chong to frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Kai and Yu Chun echoed him until the emperor reassigned Chong as Guanzhong area commander.

sentences.zh: 充納女于太子，乃止。

translations.literal: Chong married his daughter to the crown prince, and [the transfer] then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Chong betrothed his daughter to the crown prince, so the transfer was cancelled.

sentences.zh: 平吳之後，帝方修太平之化，每延公卿，與論政道。

translations.literal: After Wu fell the emperor cultivated Great Peace, hosting ministers to debate policy.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying Wu opened seminars on governance.

sentences.zh: 楷陳三五之風，次敘漢魏盛衰之跡。

translations.literal: Kai traced the Three August Ones and Five Lords, then Han and Wei's rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured on antiquity's golden ages versus Han-Wei cycles.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，坐者嘆服焉。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him; listeners sighed admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved and the assembly marveled.

sentences.zh: 楷子瓚娶楊駿女，然楷素輕駿，與之不平。

translations.literal: Kai's son Zan married Yang Jun's daughter though Kai despised Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's marriage to Jun's daughter strained Kai's contempt for Jun.

sentences.zh: 駿既執政，乃轉為衛尉，遷太子少師，優遊無事，默如也。

translations.literal: Once Jun dominated court, Kai became minister of guards and junior tutor—idle, mute.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sidelined him as ceremonial tutor with nothing to do.

sentences.zh: 及駿誅，楷以婚親收付廷尉，將加法。

translations.literal: When Jun fell, Kai as in-law went to the Ministry of Justice for sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's purge dragged Kai toward execution.

sentences.zh: 是日事倉卒，誅戮縱橫，眾人為之震恐。

translations.literal: That day slaughter raced everywhere—courtiers panicked.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden killings terrified Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 楷容色不變，舉動自若，索紙筆與親故書。

translations.literal: Kai never flinched; calmly he borrowed brush and wrote farewell letters.
translations.idiomatic: He calmly penned letters while awaiting death.

sentences.zh: 賴侍中傅祗救護得免，猶坐去官。

translations.literal: Thanks to Palace Attendant Fu Zhi's rescue he escaped execution, though he still lost office for it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi intervened; Kai merely lost rank.

sentences.zh: 太保衛瓘、太宰亮稱楷貞正不阿附，宜蒙爵土，乃封臨海侯，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: Grand tutors Wei Guan and Sima Liang praised Kai's integrity—he deserved a fief—and named him Marquis of Linhai with two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan and Sima Liang restored him as marquis of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 代楚王瑋為北軍中候，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He replaced Prince Chu Wei as colonel of the northern armies plus supernumerary attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He took the northern army colonelcy alongside attendant honors.

sentences.zh: 瑋怨瓘、亮斥己任楷，楷聞之，不敢拜，轉為尚書。

translations.literal: Wei resented Guan and Liang for ousting him for Kai; Kai declined the post and became minister of state.
translations.idiomatic: Wei blamed Kai for stealing his command; Kai fled upward to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 楷長子輿先娶亮女，女適衛瓘子，楷慮內難未已，求出外鎮，除安南將軍、假節、都督荊州諸軍事，垂當發而瑋果矯詔誅亮、瓘。

translations.literal: Kai's heir Yu had married Sima Liang's daughter while Yu's wife joined Wei Guan's son—fearing civil war Kai sought a province; made southern commander with staff for Jingzhou—just as he prepared to march, Wei forged an edict killing Liang and Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage ties to both factions drove Kai toward Jingzhou—Wei's forged orders struck first.

sentences.zh: 瑋以楷前奪己中候，又與亮、瓘婚親，密遣討楷。

translations.literal: Wei because Kai had earlier displaced him from Central Commander and was also marriage kin to Liang and Guan secretly sent forces against Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent killers after Kai for family links to his victims.

sentences.zh: 楷素知瑋有望于己，聞有變，單車入城，匿于妻父王渾家，與亮小子一夜八徙，故得免難。

translations.literal: Kai had always known Wei bore him ill will; hearing of the upheaval, he drove alone into the city and hid in his father-in-law Wang Hun's house; with Liang's youngest son he moved eight times in one night—thus he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: He dodged patrols by hiding with Wang Hun and Liang's orphan.

sentences.zh: 瑋既伏誅，以楷為中書令，加侍中，與張華、王戎並管機要。

translations.literal: After Wei died Kai directed the palace secretariat with Zhang Hua and Wang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei fell and Kai joined Zhang Hua and Wang Rong at power's core.

sentences.zh: 楷有渴利疾，不樂處勢。

translations.literal: Kai suffered wasting thirst and loathed heavy responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Diabetes-like thirst made central office unbearable.

sentences.zh: 王渾為楷請曰：「楷受先帝拔擢之恩，復蒙陛下寵遇，誠竭節之秋也。

translations.literal: Wang Hun memorialized: "Kai received favor from the late emperor's elevation and again encounters Your Majesty's grace—this is truly the season to exhaust loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun pleaded that Kai deserved lighter duty despite imperial debt.

sentences.zh: 然楷性不競於物，昔為常侍，求出為河內太守；

translations.literal: Yet Kai's nature does not strive against things; once when Palace Attendant he sought to go out as Governor of Henei;
translations.idiomatic: Kai had sought Henei while an attendant,

sentences.zh: 後為侍中，復求出為河南尹；

translations.literal: later as Palace Attendant again sought to go out as Governor of Henan;
translations.idiomatic: then pressed for Henan,

sentences.zh: 與楊駿不平，求為衛尉；

translations.literal: at odds with Yang Jun he sought to become Minister of the Palace Guards;
translations.idiomatic: then asked for the palace guard ministry against Jun,

sentences.zh: 及轉東宮，班在時類之下，安於淡退，有識有以見其心也。

translations.literal: when transferred to the Eastern Palace his rank fell below contemporaries—he rested content in quiet withdrawal; those with insight could thereby see his heart.
translations.idiomatic: and accepted junior tutor rank without envy—proof of modest intent.

sentences.zh: 楷今委頓，臣深憂之。

translations.literal: Kai is now worn down; your servant deeply worries for him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun warned the emperor that Kai was failing.

sentences.zh: 光祿勳缺，以為可用。

translations.literal: The Household Grandee post stands vacant—I believe he could fill it.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed the cushioned Household Grandee sinecure.

sentences.zh: 今張華在中書，王戎在尚書，足舉其契，無為復令楷入，名臣不多，當見將養，不違其志，要其遠濟之益。

translations.literal: Now Zhang Hua is in the Palace Secretariat and Wang Rong in the Department of State Affairs—sufficient to grasp the essentials; there is no need again to put Kai in [central office]; outstanding ministers are few—he ought to be convalesced and nurtured, not opposed in his intent; what matters is the benefit of keeping him for future aid.
translations.idiomatic: Keep Kai rested while Zhang and Wang ran policy—the plea went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 」不聽，就加光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: [The emperor] did not listen; [Kai] was additionally given Household Grandee and allowed to maintain a separate headquarters with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The throne instead piled on Household Grandee and three-duke parity.

sentences.zh: 及疾篤，詔遣黃門郎王衍省疾，楷回眸矚之曰：「竟未相識。

translations.literal: When his illness grew grave, an edict sent Huangmen Gentleman Wang Yan to inquire after his illness; Kai turned his gaze and stared at him, saying, "To the end we never met."
translations.idiomatic: The dying Kai told Wang Yan they had never met—then stared him down.

sentences.zh: 衍深歎其神俊。

translations.literal: Yan deeply sighed at his spiritual brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Yan stood awed by that dying brilliance.

sentences.zh: 楷有知人之鑒，初在河南，樂廣僑居郡界，未知名，楷見而奇之，致之於宰府。

translations.literal: Kai had a gift for judging men; when first in Henan, Yue Guang sojourned within the commandery and was not yet known—Kai saw him, thought him extraordinary, and introduced him to the minister's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He discovered Yue Guang before fame.

sentences.zh: 嘗目夏侯玄云「肅肅如入宗廟中，但見禮樂器」，鍾會「如觀武庫森森，但見矛戟在前」，傅嘏「汪翔靡所不見」，山濤「若登山臨下，幽然深遠」。

translations.literal: Once he appraised Xiahou Xuan as "solemn as entering an ancestral temple—ritual vessels alone in view"; Zhong Hui as "like viewing an arsenal bristling—spears and halberds foremost"; Fu Gu as "vast and soaring—nothing he does not survey"; Shan Tao as "like climbing a height and looking down—remote and profound."
translations.idiomatic: His portraits compared Xiahou Xuan to ritual bells, Zhong Hui to weapon racks, Fu Gu to soaring flight, Shan Tao to commanding vistas.

sentences.zh: 初，楷家炊黍在甑，或變如拳，或作血，或作蕪菁子。

translations.literal: At first, millet was steaming in Kai's kitchen steamer; some [grains] changed to fist shapes, some to blood, some to turnip seeds.
translations.idiomatic: Omens spoiled his grain—fists, blood, turnip seeds.

sentences.zh: 其年而卒，時年五十五，諡曰元。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged fifty-five; posthumous title Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died the same year at fifty-five as Marquis Yuan.

sentences.zh: 有五子：輿、瓚、憲、禮、遜。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Yu, Zan, Xian, Li, Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yu, Zan, Xian, Li, and Xun.

sentences.zh: 輿字祖明。

translations.literal: Yu, courtesy name Zuming.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yu bore the style Zuming.

sentences.zh: 少襲父爵，官至散騎侍郎，卒諡曰簡。

translations.literal: In youth he inherited his father's noble rank; he reached Supernumerary Gentleman of the Palace and died; posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded early, died as supernumerary gentleman Jian.
