sentences.zh: 瓚字國寶，中書郎，風神高邁，見者皆敬之。

translations.literal: Zan, courtesy name Guobao, was Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; his bearing was lofty and transcendent; all who saw him revered him.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao Zan awed onlookers from the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 特為王綏所重，每從其遊。

translations.literal: Wang Sui especially esteemed him and constantly accompanied him on outings.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui constantly shadowed Zan.

sentences.zh: 綏父戎謂之曰：「國寶初不來，汝數往，何也？

translations.literal: Sui's father Rong said to him: "Guobao never comes to you—why do you go to him so often?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong wondered why Sui chased a host who never called.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「國寶雖不知綏，綏自知國寶。

translations.literal: [Sui] replied: "Though Guobao does not know Sui, Sui knows Guobao."
translations.idiomatic: "He need not notice me," Sui said, "I notice him."

sentences.zh: 」楊駿之誅，為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: When Yang Jun was executed, [Zan] was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's purge left Zan dead among the soldiers.

translations.literal: The received text gives a lone equals sign between subsections.
translations.idiomatic: Another equals sign introduces the next Pei scion.

sentences.zh: 楷子憲

translations.literal: Kai's son Xian
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xian

sentences.zh: =憲字景思。

translations.literal: Xian, courtesy name Jingsi.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xian, style Jingsi,

sentences.zh: 少而穎悟，好交輕俠。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and perceptive; he loved association and light chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant boy, he chased gallantry.

sentences.zh: 及弱冠，更折節嚴重，修尚儒學，足不逾閾者數年。

translations.literal: By adulthood he had reformed to solemn dignity and cultivated Confucian learning; for several years his feet did not cross the threshold.
translations.idiomatic: He sobered into scholarship and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 陳郡謝鯤、潁川庾敳皆俊郎士也，見而奇之，相謂曰：「裴憲鯁亮宏達，通機識命，不知其何如父；

translations.literal: Xie Kun of Chen commandery and Yu Ai of Yingchuan were both outstanding gentlemen; seeing him they thought him remarkable and said to each other: "Pei Xian is upright, bright, and magnanimous—he comprehends fortune and fate—we do not know how he compares to his father;
translations.idiomatic: Xie Kun and Yu Ai praised his integrity and depth versus his father,

sentences.zh: 至於深弘保素，不以世物嬰心者，其殆過之。」

translations.literal: as for deeply preserving plain simplicity and not letting worldly matters burden his heart—perhaps in that he surpasses him."
translations.idiomatic: yet his quiet integrity may exceed the older Pei's.

sentences.zh: 初，侍講東宮，曆黃門吏部郎、侍中。

translations.literal: At first he lectured in the Eastern Palace and successively served as Huangmen, Director of Personnel, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from tutor through Huangmen and personnel to attendant.

sentences.zh: 東海王越以為豫州刺史、北中郎將、假節。

translations.literal: Prince Donghai Yue made him Governor of Yuzhou, General Who Pacifies the North, and Bearer of Staff of Authority.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue sent him to Yuzhou as northern commander with staff.

sentences.zh: 王浚承制，以憲為尚書。

translations.literal: Wang Jun by imperial mandate made Xian Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun's mandate elevated him to minister.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，王浚為石勒所破，棗嵩等莫不謝罪軍門，貢賂交錯，惟憲及荀綽恬然私室。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia, Wang Jun was broken by Shi Le; Zao Song and the rest all apologized at the army gate with tribute crisscrossing—only Xian and Xun Chuo remained tranquil in private chambers.
translations.idiomatic: When Le crushed Jun, officials rushed to abase themselves—Xian and Xun Chuo stayed dignified.

sentences.zh: 勒素聞其名，召而謂之曰：「王浚虐暴幽州，人鬼同疾。

translations.literal: Le had long heard his fame and summoned him, saying to him: "Wang Jun cruelly tyrannized Youzhou—men and ghosts alike hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Le cited Jun's cruelty to Youzhou,

sentences.zh: 孤恭行乾憲，拯茲黎元，羈舊咸歡，慶謝交路。

translations.literal: I respectfully enact Heaven's punishment and rescue these black-haired people; old bonds all rejoice, gratitude and thanks crowd the roads.
translations.idiomatic: claimed Heaven's mandate to rescue commoners,

sentences.zh: 二君齊惡傲威，誠信岨絕，防風之戮，將誰歸乎？

translations.literal: You two lordlings despised my awesome might with arrogance—your sincerity cut off—upon whom shall the punishment that befell Fangfeng fall?"
translations.idiomatic: and threatened the Fangfeng-style fate for defiant nobles.

sentences.zh: 」憲神色侃然，泣而對曰：「臣等世荷晉榮，恩遇隆重。

translations.literal: Xian's expression was stern and upright; weeping he replied: "Your servants for generations have borne Jin's glory; grace and favor were heavy."
translations.idiomatic: Xian wept yet answered that Jin had long favored his house.

sentences.zh: 王浚凶粗醜正，尚晉之遺籓。

translations.literal: Wang Jun is brutal, coarse, and deviates from rectitude, yet he remains a surviving vassal of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun remains Jin's coarse frontier lord—brutal yet nominally our man.

sentences.zh: 雖欣聖化，義岨誠心。

translations.literal: Though I rejoice in sagely transformation, duty and sincerity stand blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Even savoring your sage rule, integrity bars easy surrender.

sentences.zh: 且武王伐紂，表商容之閭，未聞商容在倒戈之例也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when King Wu attacked Zhou, he marked Shang Rong's lane with honor—I have never heard Shang Rong counted among those who reversed their spears.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu honored Shang Rong's lane after conquering Yin—no sage minister belongs with spear-turning traitors.

sentences.zh: 明公既不欲以道化厲物，必于刑忍為治者，防風之戮，臣之分也。

translations.literal: If, my lord, you will not transform the realm through the Way and insist on ruling through cruel punishments, then let Fangfeng's execution be this subject's allotted fate.
translations.idiomatic: If you reject the Way for terror tactics, treat me like executed Fangfeng.

sentences.zh: 請就辟有司。

translations.literal: I beg to be delivered to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: I ask the judiciary to take me.

sentences.zh: 」不拜而出。

translations.literal: " He refused appointment and walked out.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the post and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 勒深嘉之，待以賓禮。

translations.literal: Le praised him deeply and treated him with the courtesy due a guest.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le honored him as a guest.

sentences.zh: 勒乃簿王浚官寮親屬，皆貲至巨萬，惟憲與荀綽家有書百餘帙，鹽米各十數斛而已。

translations.literal: Le then audited Wang Jun's officials and kin—all had piled treasure to the tens of millions; only Xian and Xun Chuo had households with a hundred-odd bundles of books and only several dozen hu each of salt and rice.
translations.idiomatic: Le inventoried Jun's corrupt circle—only Xian and Chuo owned books and handfuls of grain instead of piled gold.

sentences.zh: 勒聞之，謂其長史張賓曰：「名不虛也。

translations.literal: When Le heard this, he said to his chief clerk Zhang Bin: "The reputation is no empty boast.
translations.idiomatic: Le told Zhang Bin the gossip understated their worth.

sentences.zh: 吾不喜得幽州，喜獲二子。

translations.literal: I am not pleased to have taken Youzhou—I am pleased to have gained these two men."
translations.idiomatic: He prized two Jin gentlemen more than Youzhou itself.

sentences.zh: 」署從事中郎，出為長樂太守。

translations.literal: " He appointed him attendant for executive affairs and sent him out as Governor of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Le named him staff adviser and governor of Changle.

sentences.zh: 及勒僭號，未遑制度，與王波為之撰朝儀，於是憲章文物，擬于王者。

translations.literal: When Le assumed a usurping title, before institutions were in place, he and Wang Bo drafted court ritual for him, whereupon statutes, regalia, and implements rivaled a true king's.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Zhao began court ritual, Xian and Wang Bo drafted ceremonies fit for emperors.

sentences.zh: 勒大悅，署太中大夫，遷司徒。

translations.literal: Le was greatly pleased, appointed him Grand Palace Counselor, then Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Le made him grand counselor, then minister of education.

sentences.zh: 及季龍之世，彌加禮重。

translations.literal: Under Shihu's reign he received still greater ritual honor.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu later elevated him further.

sentences.zh: 憲有二子：挹、㲄，並以文才知名。

translations.literal: Xian had two sons, Yi and Gu, both famed for literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Gu inherited literary fame.

sentences.zh: 㲄仕季龍為太子中庶子、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Gu served under Shihu as Palace Mentor to the heir apparent and Supernumerary Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Gu advised Shi Hu's heir as household tutor.

sentences.zh: 挹、㲄俱豪俠耽酒，好臧否人物。

translations.literal: Yi and Gu were both swaggering bravos who drank deep and loved judging character aloud.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers drank, swaggered, and gossiped about peers.

sentences.zh: 與河間邢魚有隙，魚竊乘㲄馬奔段遼，為人所獲，魚誣㲄使己以季龍當襲鮮卑，告之為備。

translations.literal: They feuded with Xing Yu of Hejian; Yu stole Gu's horse and fled to Duan Liao, was captured, and falsely claimed Gu had sent him to warn that Shihu would soon strike the Xianbei so they should prepare.
translations.idiomatic: A stolen horse and Xing Yu's lie framed them before Duan Liao.

sentences.zh: 時季龍適謀伐遼，而與魚辭正合。

translations.literal: At the moment Shihu was indeed plotting a campaign against Liao, and Yu's story matched his suspicions.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's planned Xianbei war lent credence to the forgery.

sentences.zh: 季龍悉誅挹、㲄，憲亦坐免。

translations.literal: Shihu executed both Yi and Gu; Xian also lost office as implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Hu purged both sons and cashiered Xian.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復以為右光祿大夫、司徒、太傅，封安定郡公。

translations.literal: Before long Xian was again appointed Right Household Grandee, Minister of Education, and Grand Tutor, enfeoffed Duke of Anding commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as household grandee, minister, tutor, and duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 憲曆官無干績之稱，然在朝玄默，未嘗以物務經懷。

translations.literal: Though Xian earned no reputation for administrative feats in successive posts, at court he remained silent and never let mundane tasks burden his heart.
translations.idiomatic: He governed quietly without bustle while minds praised his virtue.

sentences.zh: 但以德重名高，動見尊禮。

translations.literal: Yet by the weight of his virtue and fame he was everywhere received with deferential ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Reputation alone won him ritual honor.

sentences.zh: 竟卒于石氏，以族人峙子邁為嗣。

translations.literal: In the end he died under the Shi clan; his clansman Zhi's son Mai was appointed heir.
translations.idiomatic: He died under Shi rule; cousin Mai continued the line.

sentences.zh: 楷長兄黎，次兄康，並知名。

translations.literal: Kai's eldest brother Li and middle brother Kang were both celebrated.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Li and Pei Kang matched their fame.

sentences.zh: 康子盾，少曆顯位。

translations.literal: Kang's son Dun in youth held prominent offices.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's son Dun rose fast.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，為徐州刺史，委任長史司馬奧。

translations.literal: During Yongjia he was Governor of Xuzhou, leaving affairs to his chief clerk Sima Ao.
translations.idiomatic: As Xuzhou governor he delegated to Sima Ao.

sentences.zh: 奧勸盾刑殺立威，大發良人為兵，有不奉法者罪便至死。

translations.literal: Ao urged Dun to instill awe through executions and conscripted commoners as soldiers in huge numbers; anyone who violated regulations faced death.
translations.idiomatic: Ao's terror tactics—mass levies and capital punishment—ruled Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 在任三年，百姓嗟怨。

translations.literal: Within three years the common people groaned with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years the people cursed them.

sentences.zh: 東海王越，盾妹夫也。

translations.literal: Prince Donghai Yue was Dun's brother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Donghai Wang Yue was Dun's brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 越既薨，騎督滿衡便引所發良人東還。

translations.literal: After Yue died, Cavalry Commander Man Heng led the conscripted commoners eastward.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue died Man Heng marched the levies east.

sentences.zh: 尋而劉元海遣將王桑、趙固向彭城，前鋒數騎至下邳，文武不堪苛政，悉皆散走，盾、奧奔淮陰，妻子為賊人所得。

translations.literal: Soon Liu Yuanhai sent generals Wang Sang and Zhao Gu toward Pengcheng; a handful of vanguard riders reached Xiapi—the officials could not endure the harsh rule and scattered; Dun and Ao fled to Huaiyin, and their wives and children were seized by raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan's vanguard reached Xiapi; officials fled harsh rule; Dun fled to Huaiyin and lost family to bandits.

sentences.zh: 奧又誘盾降趙固。

translations.literal: Ao also induced Dun to surrender to Zhao Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Ao pushed Dun toward Zhao Gu.

sentences.zh: 固妻盾女，有寵，盾向女涕泣，固遂殺之。

translations.literal: Gu's wife was Dun's daughter and enjoyed his favor; Dun wept to his daughter, whereupon Gu killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Gu slew Dun's daughter—his own wife—after Dun's tearful plea.

sentences.zh: 盾弟邵，字道期。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Shao, courtesy name Daoqi.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Shao, style Daoqi.

sentences.zh: 元帝為安東將軍，以邵為長史，王導為司馬，二人相與為深交。

translations.literal: When Yuan-di served as General of the East, he appointed Shao chief clerk alongside Wang Dao as chief administrator—the two became sworn friends.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuan-di Shao served with Wang Dao as the prince's twin pillars.

sentences.zh: 徵為太子中庶子，復轉散騎常侍，使持節、都督揚州江西淮北諸軍事、東中郎將，隨越出項，而卒於軍中。

translations.literal: Shao was summoned as mentor to the heir, then made Supernumerary Palace Attendant, Bearer of Staff, Area Commander of all military affairs west of the Yangzi and north of the Huai in Yangzhou, and General of the East Center; he followed Yue to Xiang and died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: He died with Yue's army after tutor and Yangzhou commands.

sentences.zh: 及王導為司空，既拜，歎曰：「裴道期、劉王喬在，吾不得獨登此位。

translations.literal: When Wang Dao became Minister of Works, after taking his seat he sighed: "Were Pei Daoqi and Liu Wangqiao still alive, I could not have climbed to this office alone."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao mourned that Pei Shao and Liu Tan had vacated the seat before him.

sentences.zh: 」導子仲豫與康同字，導思舊好，乃改為敬豫焉。

translations.literal: Dao's son Zhongyu shared Kang's courtesy name; Dao, cherishing old ties, renamed him Jingyu.
translations.idiomatic: Dao renamed a son to avoid clashing with Pei Kang's style.

sentences.zh: 楷弟綽，字季舒，器宇宏曠，官至黃門侍郎、長水校尉。

translations.literal: Kai's younger brother Chuo, courtesy name Jishu, had a vast, open manner and rose to Palace Attendant and Colonel of the Long River Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo rose to palace gates and the Long River corps.

sentences.zh: 綽子遐，善言玄理，音辭清暢，泠然若琴瑟。

translations.literal: Chuo's son Xia excelled at expounding arcane principles; his tone was lucid and flowing, cool and pure as zithers and lutes.
translations.idiomatic: Xia's qingtan equaled music in clarity.

sentences.zh: 嘗與河南郭象談論，一坐嗟服。

translations.literal: Once he debated Guo Xiang of Henan—the whole assembly sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He once silenced a hall debating Guo Xiang.

sentences.zh: 又嘗在平東將軍周馥坐，與人圍棋。

translations.literal: Again, seated with General Pacifying the East Zhou Fu, he was playing weiqi with another.
translations.idiomatic: At Pacifying the East Zhou Fu's headquarters he played weiqi with companions.

sentences.zh: 馥司馬行酒，遐未即飲，司馬醉怒，因曳遐墮地。

translations.literal: Fu's major passed the wine; Xia did not drink immediately; the major, drunk and furious, dragged Xia and threw him down.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu's major passed wine, Xia hesitated; drunk and furious, the man dragged him from the mat.

sentences.zh: 遐徐起還坐，顏色不變，復棋如故。

translations.literal: Xia slowly rose, returned to his seat, his color unchanged, and resumed the game.
translations.idiomatic: He rose slowly, resumed his seat without changing color, and continued the game.

sentences.zh: 其性虛和如此。

translations.literal: His temperament was mild and yielding to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: His cool temper matched his metaphysics.

sentences.zh: 東海王越引為主簿，後為越子毗所害。

translations.literal: Prince Donghai Yue took him as chief clerk; later Yue's son Pi murdered him.
translations.idiomatic: Donghai heir Pi executed him.

sentences.zh: 初，裴、王二族盛于魏晉之世，時人以為八裴方八王：徽比王祥，楷比王衍，康比王綏，綽比王澄，瓚比王敦，遐比王導，頠比王戎，邈比王玄雲。

translations.literal: At first the Pei and Wang houses flourished side by side in the Wei-Jin age; contemporaries likened eight Peis to eight Wangs: Wei to Wang Xiang, Kai to Wang Yan, Kang to Wang Sui, Chuo to Wang Cheng, Zan to Wang Dun, Xia to Wang Dao, Yi to Wang Rong, and Miao to Wang Xuanyun.
translations.idiomatic: Wei-Jin society paired eight Peis with eight Wangs like paired stars.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historian's appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Section heading for editorial judgement.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：周稱多士，漢曰得人，取類星象，頡頏符契。

translations.literal: The historians say: Zhou praised "many shi"; Han spoke of "gaining men"—they classified types like constellations and matched tally halves.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin historians compare worthy ministers to Zhou's host of talents and Han's knack for personnel.

sentences.zh: 時乏名流，多以幹翮相許，自家光國，豈陳騫之謂歟！

translations.literal: When distinguished figures were few, men mostly traded praise of administrative talent—thinking to glorify house and state—is this not precisely what Chen Qian meant!
translations.idiomatic: They hint Chen Qian embodied vain ministerial boasting.

sentences.zh: 秀則聲蓋朋僚，稱為領袖。

translations.literal: As for Xiu, his voice overshadowed peers and he was called their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiu led his generation.

sentences.zh: 楷則機神幼發，目以清通。

translations.literal: As for Kai, wit and spirit stirred early and observers dubbed him lucid and penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kai earned his reputation for enlightened clarity.

sentences.zh: 俱為晉氏名臣，良有以也。

translations.literal: Together they stood as Jin's celebrated ministers—and rightly so.
translations.idiomatic: They deserved Jin's esteem.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：世既順才，才膺世至。

translations.literal: The encomium runs: The age bows to talent; talent rises to meet the age.
translations.idiomatic: The verse praises timely union of talent and age.

sentences.zh: 高平沈敏，蘊茲名器。

translations.literal: Gaoping's Chen Qian was deep and astute, cherishing those vessels of fame.
translations.idiomatic: It salutes Chen Qian's steady grasp of power.

sentences.zh: 钜鹿自然，亦云經笥。

translations.literal: Julu's Pei Xiu moved with natural ease—another walking library of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: It salutes Pei Xiu's effortless scholarship.

sentences.zh: 媧皇煉石，晉圖開秘。

translations.literal: The goddess Nüwa smelted stone to mend heaven; Jin's charts unlocked hidden treasure.
translations.idiomatic: It invokes myth and charts to praise Jin mapping.

sentences.zh: 頠有清規，承家來媚。

translations.literal: Yi upheld pure standards, inheriting grace for his house.
translations.idiomatic: It closes by honoring Pei Yi's integrity.
